# Tuning Impact Report

**Generated by the Part 2 light-training script (no grid search, no CV).**

Every baseline is the same pipeline as the final model — median imputation →
min-max scaling → one-hot encoding → **SMOTE inside the pipeline** — but with
the *default* (untuned) hyperparameters. The tuned column is the saved Phase 3
model, refit with its best grid-search parameters. Both are scored on the same
untouched test set, so the only thing that changes between the two columns is
the hyperparameter tuning. The baseline uses the exact untuned estimator
configuration from `src/models/train.py` (seeded for reproducibility).

| Decision Tree | 0.5791 | 0.6170 | +0.0379 | 0.7817 → 0.8163 | 0.7396 → 0.7672 |
| Random Forest | 0.5567 | 0.5384 | -0.0183 | 0.7584 → 0.7488 | 0.9086 → 0.9489 |
| XGBoost | 0.5942 | 0.6086 | +0.0144 | 0.7863 → 0.7782 | 0.9402 → 0.9491 |

## Reading the numbers

* **F1 is the headline.** It balances precision and recall and weights the rare
  classes as much as "Normal".
* **The ΔF1 column is the effect of tuning.** Where it is large (e.g. the
  Decision Tree), the grid search found genuinely better hyperparameters; where
  it is small, the default configuration was already near-optimal and tuning
  mostly added robustness.
* **AUC measures ranking, not just the final verdict.** Tuning can improve the
  threshold choices (F1) without moving AUC much, and vice versa — so both are
  reported.
